key_value_text.quote: the number of light neutrino species is found to be Nv=3.27±0.30. this results rules out of the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL.
key_value_text.value: Number of light neutrino species reported in the four first LEP papers: ALEPH Nν = 3.27 ± 0.30 (the ALEPH abstract says this rules out the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL); L3 3.42 ± 0.48; DELPHI 2.4 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst); OPAL 3.1 ± 0.4. The final LEP+SLD combination (2005) gives 2.9840 ± 0.0082.

name: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species
notes: This entity records the historic 1989 determinations of the number of light neutrino species; the final precision value (2.9840+/-0.0082, LEP+SLD, arXiv:hep-ex/0509008) is recorded separately as result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006 and is no longer used as this record's key_value (a review found it read as the 1989 result). date/date_kind reflect the 1989 papers.

ALEPH's own paper title is used as claim.quote because it states the result plainly ('Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species'); L3, DELPHI and OPAL used different titles for the same Z-lineshape analysis (see key_value_text).

Other 1989 abstracts (verbatim): L3 — "We also determined Γinvisible=0.567±0.080 GeV, corresponding to 3.42±0.48 number of neutrino flavors." (Phys. Lett. B 231, 509; https://collaborate.princeton.edu/en/publications/a-determination-of-the-properties-of-the-neutral-intermediate-vec/). DELPHI — "A two-parameter fit in the framework of the standard model yields for the number of light neutrino species Nν=2.4±0.4 (stat.) ±0.5 (syst.)" (Phys. Lett. B 231, 539; https://difusion.ulb.ac.be/vufind/Record/ULB-DIPOT:oai:dipot.ulb.ac.be:2013/116538/TOC). OPAL — "In the context of the standard model t these results imply 3.1 ± 0.4 neutrino generations." (Phys. Lett. B 231, 530; https://researchconnect.stonybrook.edu/en/publications/measurement-of-the-zsup0sup-mass-and-width-with-the-opal-detector/).

summary.plain: The four LEP experiments each measured the Z boson resonance and inferred the number of light neutrino species: ALEPH 3.27 ± 0.30, L3 3.42 ± 0.48, DELPHI 2.4 ± 0.4 ± 0.5, OPAL 3.1 ± 0.4. ALEPH states that, within the standard electroweak model, its result rules out a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% confidence.
summary.technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL each reported a number of light neutrino species from their 1989 Z-resonance measurements (Phys. Lett. B 231, 509-547): ALEPH Nν = 3.27 ± 0.30 within the constraints of the standard electroweak model ("rules out the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL"); L3 3.42 ± 0.48 (from Γinvisible = 0.567 ± 0.080 GeV); DELPHI 2.4 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) from a two-parameter standard-model fit; OPAL 3.1 ± 0.4 in the context of the standard model. The final LEP+SLD combination, Nν = 2.9840 ± 0.0082, was published later (Phys. Rept. 427, 2006).

title: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species
why_it_matters: ALEPH's abstract states that its result rules out the possibility of a fourth type of light neutrino at 98% CL, within the constraints of the standard electroweak model. Fermilab's 2000 announcement of the tau neutrino says that in 1989 experimenters at CERN found proof that the tau neutrino is the third and last light neutrino of the Standard Model.
